rules.forbids: forbids: adding to the crisis basket when all its channels are already traversed
rules.rule_text: late in a crisis the neglected side is resolution; when every channel is priced for continuation the unpriced asymmetry is de-escalation

rules.forbids: forbids: conditioning an offtake or force majeure call on which unit burned; forbids assuming a fuels-unit fire leaves the chemical side supplying
rules.rule_text: a fire in one unit of an integrated site stops deliveries of unrelated products; the offtaker's force majeure names the site, not the unit

rules.forbids: forbids: a falsifier that fires on commentary for a claim about prices; forbids reading a 'deepens congestion' headline as a price move
rules.rule_text: narrative and price diverge after a small shock: trade press narrates congestion the indices do not show; a price call must name the price series and nothing else in its falsifier

rules.forbids: forbids: remaining suppliers' spreads staying flat after a peer outage in a region-locked market
rules.rule_text: when one supplier of a region-locked product is removed, the remaining suppliers capture the spread

rules.forbids: forbids: predicting a large sustained equity loss for a diversified owner from one unit outage absent casualties or liability
rules.rule_text: the named victim of an event is over-attended relative to its earnings impact; single-unit losses at diversified owners are equity noise

rules.forbids: forbids: waiting for price prints to confirm a plant outage when a force majeure letter is available
rules.rule_text: a producer's force majeure declaration is the fastest public carrier of a plant outage, preceding every price print

rules.forbids: forbids: ignoring the co-product when scoping a plant outage
rules.rule_text: a plant that co-produces two products cuts both when it stops; the second product is named later than the first

rules.forbids: forbids: predicting feedstock tightening from a consumer outage
rules.rule_text: a large consumer of a feedstock going offline softens that feedstock at the margin

rules.forbids: forbids: long-rival/short-owner where the owner holds sister plants on the same node
rules.rule_text: the wounded owner of the substitutes collects its own scarcity premium; when the victim also owns remaining capacity the competitor's gift self-cancels

rules.forbids: forbids: predicting a stock move without comparing event earnings impact to concurrent macro variance on the same name
rules.rule_text: equity visibility equals event size divided by ambient tide; below a ratio to be measured there is no trace to trade

rules.forbids: forbids: the round-2 pre-lock prediction set
rules.rule_text: a plant outage in a region-locked concentrated product with an owner holding sister plants: force majeure arrives first, derivatives reprice larger than the parent, the co-product reprices only if its market is tight, and the owner's equity shows nothing

rules.forbids: forbids: assuming nameplate unit count, and therefore partial-site continuity, at an asset recently bought out of insolvency
rules.rule_text: a plant revived from insolvency runs fewer units than its nameplate; an outage there takes the whole site, not one unit

rules.forbids: forbids: expecting a force majeure letter as the fast public carrier for a contracted power plant; the notice goes to one counterparty and is not published
rules.rule_text: where offtake is a bilateral utility contract, the outage's first public carrier is the owner's quarterly disclosure, not a force majeure notice

rules.forbids: forbids: reading a null fuel-market response as evidence of slack when product loadings were already stopped for another reason
rules.rule_text: a pre-existing logistics stop masks an outage; when loadings are already halted the fuels market cannot see the unit go down

rules.forbids: forbids: scoring a commodity or equity leg as attributable when a larger concurrent driver set the price; forbids reading a null response under a tide as slack
rules.rule_text: a tide sets the price of everything it touches; an event under it is visible only in what the tide does not price

rules.forbids: forbids: downstream derivative prices being unaffected by an upstream regional shutdown
rules.rule_text: when a large producing region is shut, its exports vanish and the chain downstream reprices in the order of substitution difficulty

rules.forbids: forbids: treating the commodity price as the earliest signal of a chokepoint or plant event
rules.rule_text: the toll booth learns before the cargo; constraint prices (insurance, freight, allocation) reprice before the commodity they gate

rules.forbids: forbids: a lasting operational or cost constraint on peer plants arising from a post-accident inspection order
rules.rule_text: a fatal industrial accident triggers a jurisdiction-wide inspection order within weeks that binds nothing durable on peers

rules.forbids: forbids: treating a chemical plant as unexposed to a refinery it is not co-located with; forbids assuming the link is priced before the notice
rules.rule_text: a single-supplier feedstock link is a hidden node; the downstream plant's force majeure is the first public statement of the link

factor_resolutions.note: The only description is a gas release igniting while contractors deblocked a pipeline during heat-treatment work, with no explosion; nothing states whether the reactor, extrusion train or only ancillary piping was damaged. Binding factor unobserved.

A prohibition notice was issued on 23 Jul, so the factor's falsifier (no notice) did not fire, but the notice as reported stops the activities that led to the fire rather than the unit outright, and nothing shows when it was lifted; the lag band cannot be read.

No source says anything about the cracker or the ethylene pipeline; the ignition was in a pipeline being deblocked at Poly 3, but which line is not stated, so neither the days estimate nor the months falsifier is observed.
No restart announcement of any kind appears, so neither an investigation-linked restart nor the falsifier (restart announced without reference to an investigation) can be seen.
The seat of the fire is described as a pipeline under deblocking, not the finishing lines, but no source addresses the extrusion and pelletising lines or their restart.

evidence.title: Mail & Guardian, 24 Jul 2026: Labour department investigates fire after three workers injured at Sasolburg plant
evidence.excerpt: Fire at about 13:04 on Tuesday (21 Jul) at Sasol's Poly 3 polyethylene facility, Midland site, Sasolburg: a gas release ignited while contractors were deblocking a pipeline during heat-treatment work. Three contractor employees burned, one in ICU. Sasol: no explosion; Poly 3 unit shut down pending investigation; no risk to communities. Department of Employment and Labour issued a prohibition notice (Thursday) stopping the activities that led to the fire until it is satisfied work can resume.

evidence.title: FX Leaders, 23 Jul 2026: Sasol share price breaks out after FY26 targets are met; reclaims R200 as oil prices surge
evidence.excerpt: The 23 Jul surge is attributed to FY26 production and sales targets being met, rising oil on Middle East tensions, and the PIC lifting its stake to 20.2% on 13 Jul. A 28 Jul follow-up attributes the retreat below R200 to the oil rally fading and Hormuz tensions easing. Neither piece mentions the Sasolburg fire (page returns 403; content from search-engine summaries of both articles).

evidence.title: Sasol business performance metrics for the year ended 30 June 2026 (released 21 Jul 2026, the event day)
evidence.excerpt: South African Polymers sales FY26 1,241kt (FY25 1,195kt), 42% of Base Chemicals. Secunda highest annual production in five years; safety performance in Q4 'encouraging' after two fatalities earlier in FY26. Force majeure in the period only in International Chemicals on ME-constrained feedstocks. Nothing on Sasolburg polyethylene (the fire post-dates the period; the release is the same morning).

evidence.title: Sasol FY26 results presentation script, 1 Sep 2026
evidence.excerpt: p6: 'We again had no major process safety incidents' (FY26, to 30 Jun). p20: impairment of the South African Polyethylene CGU 'due to a stronger forecast rand exchange rate and a lower long-term Polyethylene pricing outlook'. No mention of Sasolburg Poly 3, the July fire, a prohibition notice, a restart, or force majeure on polymers anywhere in 33 pages.

evidence.title: Sasol additional information for analysts FY26, 1 Sep 2026
evidence.excerpt: p22 Chemicals Africa: 'Sales volumes increased by 5% ... supported by improved production at SO and Sasolburg. Outlook: Sales volumes for 2027 are expected to be 0-5% higher than 2026, supported by improved production at SO and Sasolburg operations.' Polyethylene CGU impairment R3.7bn (FX and long-term price). Force majeure mentioned only for International Chemicals feedstocks. No mention of the Poly 3 fire, a restart date, or polymer force majeure.

evidence.title: Coverage record, retrieved 7 Sep 2026: no South Africa PE / Sasol / force majeure item found
evidence.excerpt: ChemOrbis Africa page shows no South Africa, Sasol, Safripol or PE headline for Jul-Sep 2026 in its free view. Searches for 'Sasol force majeure polyethylene', 'sales allocation', 'Poly 3 restart', 'prohibition notice lifted', Plastics SA and Engineering News polymer items, and local Vaal papers returned nothing after the 24 Jul M&G piece. ICIS is paywalled. Coverage on restart, force majeure and local PE pricing is thin.

evidence.title: Vaal Triangle Info: Sasol Polymers Sasolburg Midland site capacity
evidence.excerpt: Sasolburg Midland site produces polyethylene: a 100,000 t/y LDPE plant and a 150,000 t/y LLDPE plant (250 kt/y combined). Context for the size of Poly 3 relative to Sasol's 1,241 kt SA polymers sales and R61bn group EBITDA.

evidence.title: Financial Mail, 11 Jun 2026: KAP boosted by Gulf supply squeeze
evidence.excerpt: Tide: the Hormuz closure had already lifted global PE prices 50-80% by March 2026 and was boosting Safripol's parent KAP by June. Safripol runs HDPE and PP plants in Sasolburg on ethylene and propylene piped from Sasol. Any local PE price move in Jul-Aug 2026 sits on this backdrop.

resolutions.scorer_note: map miss: the plant is Sasol's Poly 3 (LDPE/LLDPE, Midland site), not Safripol's HDPE plant. The baseline (the larger operator on site) was right. The stated basis (a Sasol incident would be headlined as Sasol's) was wrong: the selector's bare wording carried no signal about the operator. Map calls carry no mechanism.

SOL vs Top40: 22 Jul -2.4pts, 23 Jul +11.9pts, 24 Jul -3.9pts; every move is attributed by the only commentary found to oil, the FY26 metrics released the morning of the fire, and the PIC stake; no source attributes any move to the fire, and Sasol's own FY26 results do not mention it. The falsifier (>3% underperformance on 22 or 23 Jul with the fire cited) did not fire. Tide: the FY26 metrics release and an oil swing dominate the window, so the fire's absence from the tape is consistent with the visibility-ratio rule but the tide alone would produce the same tape. Baseline (parent dips on the day): SOL fell 1.59% on 22 Jul, so the dumb baseline also scores a hit on the letter of its claim even though nothing attributes the dip.
conditional on Safripol being named the operator; the plant is Sasol's, so the condition never occurred. Untestable by construction; carries no rule credit or debit.
